note: Deterministic phrase patterns checked before any model call. Two reasons they exist. First, safety: a patient describing crushing chest pain radiating to the arm should not be asked five follow-up questions first. Second, availability: these fire when Gemini is unreachable, so the most dangerous presentations are still caught in DEGRADED and OFFLINE mode. Matching is plain substring matching on the lowercased message - no model, no embedding, no network. Patterns are listed in the languages the interface offers, because a red flag that only works in English is not a red flag for the patient who needs it most.

flags.label: Unable to breathe
flags.rationale: The patient reports being unable to breathe. This is treated as severe respiratory distress without waiting for further questions.

flags.label: Crushing or radiating chest pain
patterns: chest pain going down my arm
pain in my chest and arm
tightness in my chest and jaw
flags.rationale: The description matches a classic acute coronary syndrome pattern. Assessment is not delayed for further history.

flags.label: Loss of consciousness
flags.rationale: Loss of consciousness has a wide differential, much of it time-critical, and is escalated immediately.

flags.label: Uncontrolled bleeding
flags.rationale: Bleeding that does not stop with pressure is immediately life-threatening.

flags.label: Fever with non-blanching rash
flags.rationale: A non-blanching rash with fever is treated as possible meningococcal sepsis.

flags.label: Stiff neck with fever
flags.rationale: Neck stiffness raises the possibility of meningitis and is assessed urgently.

flags.label: Vomiting blood
flags.rationale: Haematemesis indicates active upper gastrointestinal bleeding.

flags.label: Rigid abdomen
flags.rationale: A rigid abdomen suggests peritonitis, which is a surgical emergency.

flags.label: Head injury on blood thinners
patterns: hit my head and i take warfarin
hit my head and i'm on blood thinners
banged my head, i take apixaban
flags.rationale: Head injury while anticoagulated carries a raised risk of delayed intracranial bleeding even when the patient appears well.

flags.label: Suspected stroke
flags.rationale: The description matches a possible stroke. This falls outside the five complaints covered by this rule set, so VITA escalates it to a clinician immediately rather than triaging it.

flags.label: Self-harm or suicidal intent
flags.rationale: A mental health crisis is outside this rule set. VITA does not attempt to triage it and routes the patient to a clinician immediately.

flags.label: Pregnancy with bleeding or severe pain
flags.rationale: Obstetric emergencies require specialist assessment this rule set does not provide. Escalated rather than triaged.

flags.label: Choking or airway obstruction
flags.rationale: A possible airway obstruction is the most time-critical presentation there is.

flags.label: Object embedded in a wound
flags.rationale: An object still in the wound is penetrating trauma. It is left in place and the patient goes straight through.

flags.label: Amputation or crush injury
flags.rationale: Amputation or crush injury is time-critical and can bleed catastrophically.
